description: Fix critical security gaps in authMiddleware.js and auth.service.js (Steps A), and set up the Supabase client infrastructure (Step B): install @supabase/supabase-js, remove dead dependencies (mongoose, mongodb, sequelize, sqlite3), update env.js, create supabase.js, replace db.js connectDB() with a Supabase health check, and write the SQL migration file. These changes are a prerequisite for all service migration work.
steps: Step A1 — Fix authMiddleware.js: In Backend/src/middleware/authMiddleware.js, replace all three hardcoded admin fallbacks with `return next(ApiError.unauthorized('Authentication required.'))`. The three locations are: (1) missing/invalid Authorization header, (2) empty token or literal 'demo-token', (3) catch block for any JWT error. The requireRole() function is correct and stays unchanged.

Step A2 — Fix auth.service.js: In Backend/src/services/auth.service.js, delete the plaintext password comparison block `if (!isMatch && user.passwordHash === password) { isMatch = true; }` and delete the entire `acceptable` object and its surrounding if-block. Only bcrypt.compare should remain for password validation.

Step A3 — Fix auth.routes.js: In Backend/src/routes/auth.routes.js, add `requireRole('admin')` middleware after `authMiddleware` on both `POST /staff` and `PUT /staff/:id` routes. Import requireRole from '../middleware/authMiddleware' (already imported in the file).

Step B1 — Update package.json: In Backend/package.json, add `"@supabase/supabase-js": "^2.49.4"` to dependencies. Remove `"mongoose"`, `"mongodb"`, `"sequelize"`, `"sqlite3"` from dependencies. Run `npm install` in Backend/ to apply changes.

Step B2 — Update env.js: In Backend/src/config/env.js, add SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY to the config object from process.env. Add a startup warning if either is missing. Keep all existing fields. Remove the MONGODB_URI warning (replace with Supabase warning). Full updated file content: require dotenv, define config with all existing fields PLUS SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, warn if JWT_SECRET is default, warn if SUPABASE_URL or SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is missing in development (or exit(1) in production).

Step B3 — Create supabase.js: Create Backend/src/config/supabase.js. Use CommonJS: `const { createClient } = require('@supabase/supabase-js'); const config = require('./env'); if (!config.SUPABASE_URL || !config.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY) { throw new Error('SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY must be set'); } const supabase = createClient(config.SUPABASE_URL, config.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, { auth: { persistSession: false } }); module.exports = supabase;`

Step B4 — Replace db.js: Rewrite Backend/src/config/db.js entirely. Remove mongoose.connect() and seedDefaultData(). New connectDB(): require supabase from './supabase', do `const { error } = await supabase.from('clinics').select('id').limit(1)`, throw if error, log success. Export only { connectDB }.

Step B5 — Create migration.sql: Create Backend/src/config/migration.sql by copying the COMPLETE SQL from Section 5 of .agents/tasks/phase2-schema-design.md verbatim. This is the single source of truth for the PostgreSQL schema. The implementer must run this file in the Supabase SQL editor before any table operations.
Step B6 — Update index.js startup log: In Backend/index.js, update the console.log in startServer() to say 'Supabase connected' instead of 'MongoDB connected'. No other logic changes needed.
acceptance_criteria: Backend/src/middleware/authMiddleware.js: The catch block and both early-return paths return next(ApiError.unauthorized(...)) — no hardcoded admin identity anywhere in the file.
Backend/src/services/auth.service.js: No `acceptable` object. No plaintext comparison block. Only bcrypt.compare() used for password validation.
Backend/src/routes/auth.routes.js: POST /staff and PUT /staff/:id routes have requireRole('admin') in their middleware chain.
Backend/package.json: @supabase/supabase-js present. mongoose, mongodb, sequelize, sqlite3 absent.
Backend/src/config/supabase.js exists and exports a Supabase createClient instance.
Backend/src/config/db.js: connectDB() uses supabase.from('clinics').select('id').limit(1) health check. No mongoose references.
Backend/src/config/migration.sql: Contains complete SQL with all 19 enum types, 4 sequences, 18 tables, triggers, indexes, and RLS policies from phase2-schema-design.md Section 5.
Running `node index.js` from Backend/ with valid SUPABASE_URL/KEY and migration SQL already applied prints '[DB] Supabase connected successfully'.
verification: cd Backend && npm install — must complete without errors

node index.js from Backend/ with SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY set in Backend/.env, and migration SQL already run in Supabase — must print '[DB] Supabase connected successfully' (not a MongoDB error)

curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"admin@dwarkadental.com","password":"admin123"}' — must return 200 with JWT token (seed must also be completed; use FEAT-003's seed to confirm)
curl http://localhost:5000/api/patients (no Authorization header) — must return 401 Unauthorized (not 200 with admin access)
findings: All 8 steps completed successfully. Step A1: Replaced all three admin-bypass fallbacks in authMiddleware.js with next(ApiError.unauthorized('Authentication required.')). Step A2: Removed plaintext password comparison block and entire 'acceptable' hardcoded password object from auth.service.js — only bcrypt.compare remains. Step A3: Added requireRole('admin') to POST /staff and PUT /staff/:id in auth.routes.js; also updated import to destructure requireRole. Step B1: Updated package.json — added @supabase/supabase-js@^2.49.4, removed mongoose, mongodb, sequelize, sqlite3; npm install succeeded. Step B2: Replaced env.js — removed MONGODB_URI, added SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY with development warning / production exit(1). Step B3: Created Backend/src/config/supabase.js using createClient with persistSession:false. Step B4: Replaced db.js — connectDB() now queries supabase.from('clinics').select('id').limit(1) and logs '[DB] Supabase connected successfully'. Step B5: Created Backend/src/config/migration.sql with complete SQL (19 enums, 1 trigger function, 4 sequences, 1 helper function, 18 tables, 34 indexes, 12 triggers, 18 RLS enables, 18 RLS policies). Step B6: Updated index.js startup log from 'MongoDB connected' to 'Supabase connected'. Blockers for later FEATs: (1) auth.service.js and auth.routes.js still use Mongoose User model — FEAT-002 must migrate these to userDb. (2) Backend/.env does not yet have SUPABASE_URL/SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY — server will warn on startup and connectDB() will fail until FEAT-003 or manual env setup. (3) migration.sql must be run in Supabase SQL editor before any table operations. No issues encountered with npm install.
